title: A pickup record date on 46th Street
summary: A group from 46th Street gave him a date for Then I'll Be Happy; he explains the 46th versus 48th Street class distinction.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: recording Then I'll Be Happy? You told me about that once.

Yeah, I think I met with some group. I don't know who they were. They picked me up somewhere on Broadway and they gave me the date. It wasn't too good of a, come on, too hot. I don't know. But you didn't know the guys or anything? No, I don't know who they were. It was just some group of guys that hung down. You see, in those days there was sort of a class distinction. If you were a little bit better you hung out at 48th Street and if you were not you hung down at 46th Street. And they hung out at 46th Street. They gave me the record dates. And some of the guys, if you got a little bit up in the deal you were 48th Street boy, a different clique. I mean, you know, one of those things, just the way it was when I did.
